t12_synthetic_effect.interpretation: Extreme low-N/high-C:N synthetic qualification case; demonstrates material causal amplification but is not a field-effect estimate.

findings.summary: WOFOST81 is a discrete one-day transition system: phenology/vernalisation, root, stem, storage-organ and leaf integration contain daily state increments without delt scaling, while some top-level cumulatives do scale by delt. Non-unit delt is therefore internally inconsistent and unsupported.
DVS_Partitioning_N documentation says N stress affects partitioning, but implementation modifies root allocation with RFTRA (water/oxygen stress); no N-stress variable is used in partitioning.
Water and N uptake use different implicit spatial root activity assumptions.
Daily operator ordering determines competition among uptake, reactions and transport.
Unbounded advective export can exceed a finite NH4/NO3 pool; production transport now limits donor export and preserves internal transfer mass.
Crop N balance is checked in calc_rates before same-day rates are integrated, so it verifies the prior integrated state and may not independently check the terminal crop-day update.

Existing assimilation test constructs a driver without TMIN although current assimilation implementation requires drv.TMIN; audit CI isolates this stale harness rather than treating it as a model regression.

Requested leaf/stem reallocation is capped against a fixed start-of-reallocation quota, not same-day surviving donor biomass. Leaf integration removes nothing when REALLOC_LV >= post-senescence leaf biomass; stem integration can drive WST negative, while storage organs are still credited from requested REALLOC_SO. A transactional donor-limited repair is required.

Crop-N balance raises only at absolute checksum >= 1 kg N/ha; smaller systematic daily bookkeeping errors can pass. Qualification suite should use tighter process-level invariants even if production tolerance remains unchanged.

Direct unittest module discovery incorrectly instantiates WofostTestingTemplate and pandas 3 breaks label-based Series[0] access. Regression envelope now invokes the module's canonical suite() and uses iloc[0].

When harvest date and max_duration coincide, the baseline second independent if overwrites finish_type='harvest' with 'max_duration'. Harvest is an explicit management cause and now retains precedence.

A state event first observed exactly at its threshold is silently initialized with sign=0 and never fires unless the state subsequently crosses away and back. Exact threshold at first observation now dispatches once.

Each model day integrates rates calculated for the previous model date, then applies current-day agromanagement, then calculates current-day rates. Timed management therefore affects current-day rates but not the integration that has already occurred on that date; state-triggered events inspect post-integration current states.

Within calc_rates water balance executes before SNOMIN; within integrate water balance executes before SNOMIN. SNOMIN therefore consumes water-flow/rate information under a fixed water-first ownership order.

Engine calculates crop rates before soil rates. Crop RNuptake demand is therefore computed from NAVAIL state integrated at the start of the day, then SNOMIN consumes that same day's RNuptake. This is an explicit one-way daily lag/explicit coupling contract: soil transformations calculated later cannot revise same-day crop demand.

Crop evapotranspiration calculates TRA/WTRALY before the soil water balance calculates its current-day rates; MLWB then uses published crop extraction as a prescribed sink. The next day's crop stress sees the integrated soil state. This is an explicit daily crop-first water-demand / soil-response coupling.

Timed amendment signals are dispatched before current-day calc_rates; SNOMIN collects amendment placeholders in that calc_rates and integrates them on the next Engine integration call. Calendar labels therefore describe the rate day, while state incorporation occurs at the following integration boundary.

On END_DATE the Timer emits OUTPUT and TERMINATE before Engine integrates that date. Engine then integrates the previous day's rates, processes management and current-day rates, saves output, and terminates. Thus final-day output is post-integration but current-day rates are not subsequently integrated. END_DATE is an integration boundary, not a fully executed additional rate day.

CROP_FINISH is deferred until after crop and soil calc_rates. A crop reaching maturity during integration can therefore still execute one final current-day crop calc_rates before finalize/delete; those newly calculated rates are not integrated when the crop is deleted. Final states remain correct for the integrated transition, but final-day rates should not be interpreted as realized fluxes.

A single daily state jump may cross multiple configured thresholds. Dispatcher evaluates thresholds independently, so all crossed rising thresholds should fire once; adversarial test added to guard this behavior.

Engine deletes crop state/rate registrations recursively and forces garbage collection because signal subscriptions otherwise retain objects. New crop start is rejected while a crop object remains. No additional rotation ownership defect was established in this tranche.

Multiple apply_n_snomin events on the same rate day append organic amendment pools but baseline mineral NH4/NO3 placeholders are assigned, so each later event overwrites mineral N from earlier events. Repair accumulates mineral-N contributions.
WaterBalanceLayered._on_IRRIGATE assigns _RIRR, so multiple irrigation signals before calc_rates silently retain only the last event. Repair makes independent same-day irrigation events additive.

Rainfall and irrigation enter through distinct current-day inputs (drv.RAIN and RIRR) and are combined in infiltration/surface-water logic rather than overwriting one another. No duplicate-source defect established.

Organ uptake allocation adds donor translocation rates to leaf/root/stem uptake weights while subtracting translocation from storage-organ demand. This may intentionally replenish donor organs, but denominator remains total Ndemand without corresponding translocation terms. Requires algebraic closure test under strong simultaneous translocation, uptake and fixation before classification.
